question: A 10-year-old girl's height is 118 cm (2.5 SD below the mean for age). Her growth velocity over the past 12 months is 3 cm/yr (expected ≥5 cm/yr for age). Her father's height is 168 cm, her mother's height is 154 cm. Which statement BEST describes the correct clinical interpretation?

answers.text: Her mid-parental height target is 154 cm; a velocity of 3 cm/yr is normal for her genetic potential

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mid-parental height for a girl = (father's height + mother's height − 13 cm) ÷ 2 = (168 + 154 − 13) ÷ 2 = 154.5 cm. However, a velocity of 3 cm/yr at age 10 is well below the expected ≥5 cm/yr — this is pathologically slow and cannot be explained by genetic potential alone.

answers.text: Her mid-parental height target is ~154.5 cm; a velocity of 3 cm/yr at age 10 is pathologically slow and requires investigation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. MPH (girl) = (168 + 154 − 13) ÷ 2 = 154.5 cm (±5 cm target range). A velocity of only 3 cm/yr at age 10 is less than 5 cm/yr — pathologically slow and the most important flag for organic growth disorder (e.g. hypothyroidism, GH deficiency, systemic disease). Referral and investigation are indicated.

answers.text: Her mid-parental height target is 161 cm (using the formula for boys); slow velocity is expected because she is pre-pubertal

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The formula for girls subtracts 13 cm from the sum, whereas for boys it adds 13 cm — the boy's formula has been applied in error here. Pre-pubertal status does not justify a velocity of 3 cm/yr; the minimum expected is 5 cm/yr from age 3 to puberty.

answers.text: Growth velocity is irrelevant; only the height at a single time-point determines the need for referral

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Growth velocity is the MOST discriminating single parameter. A child may be short at one visit due to familial or constitutional factors, but a pathologically slow velocity is the hallmark of an organic disorder. A child crossing percentile lines downward must be investigated regardless of absolute height.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: MPH (girl) = (dad + mum − 13) ÷ 2; MPH (boy) = (dad + mum + 13) ÷ 2. And velocity <5 cm/yr after age 3 = investigate and refer, even if height is within normal range.

Well done. MPH formula for girls: (father's height + mother's height − 13) ÷ 2. A velocity below 5 cm/yr after age 3 — regardless of the child's actual height — is the primary flag for pathological growth and triggers referral for investigation.
